_README: Hand-maintained pricing policy for the purchasing-power price cut. This is the ONLY file in this
folder to edit by hand. `./scripts/store iap-ppp` reads it plus the Play snapshot and regenerates
ppp-plan.md and proposed/. See the `play-store-assets` skill for the full workflow.
The price of an in-scope region is its reference price (ppp-reference-prices.json) multiplied by
its tier factor, then rounded to a local price point. Scaling Play's own price rather than
converting from the anchor keeps Play's exchange rate and each region's tax treatment intact.
_anchorRegions: The full-price reference the tier factors are expressed against, read live from the snapshot. Both must stay out of scope; the script asserts it.
_products: All six tips. Each tier is sold twice (a one-off record and a repeatable twin), and both carry the same price so the tip jar shows one figure per tier.
_tiers: Tier keys must match the 'tier' values in ppp-classification.json. A region whose tier is absent
from this map keeps Play's price, which is how upper-middle and high-income regions stay at full
price. A country just above the low-income threshold pays 2.75x what one just below pays; add a
bridge tier and assign regions to it via regionTierOverrides if that cliff matters.
_regionTierOverrides: Manual region -> tier assignment on top of the World Bank band: "VN": "lower-middle" pulls a region into scope, "LB": null drops one. Every entry is listed in ppp-plan.md as a deviation.
_excludedRegions: Countries the app is not distributed in. The pricing API cannot tell, so this list records it, and the script refuses to build when it disagrees with the snapshot. Empty: all six tips are on sale in all 172 regions.
_integerCurrencyOverrides: Whether Play quotes a currency in whole units is inferred from the snapshot. The script stops when a repriced region's currency is called integer off a single price; set "XYZ": true or false here after checking the Console.
_floorUsd: No region is priced below the local equivalent of this, converted with the FX snapshot in
ppp-classification.json and snapped UP to the nearest price point. USD 0.49 is the cheapest point
on the .49/.99 grid, so prices may go under one dollar or euro in the deepest tier. Play's own
minimum is far lower (USD 0.05 / EUR 0.05), so this only stops a price from rounding to nothing.
_liftWholeRegionToFloor: When the floor binds on one tier, raise the region's other tiers by the same proportion instead of clamping each on its own, so small / medium / large keep their spread rather than collapsing onto the same price.
